questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?

options.text: It is a square blue knob.
It is a triangular yellow knob.
It is an eight-sided red knob.
It is a circular orange knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is an eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control on newer vehicles is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: It applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
It applies and releases the parking brakes.
It applies and releases the emergency brake.
It applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system. The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you use the brake pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: How should cargo inside a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no more than three feet high.
It should be secured to prevent movement.
It should be loaded with the heaviest items on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured properly to prevent it from moving during transport. Cargo should be arranged to keep the vehicle's center of gravity low and evenly distributed.

questions.question: What speed should you drive at?

options.text: Always drive at the posted speed limit.
Always drive slightly below the posted speed limit.
Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
Drive as fast as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your speed based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of fatal crashes. You must continuously adjust your speed to match current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When parking a double or triple, what type of spot should you choose?

options.text: A spot that allows you to back up when leaving.
A spot that allows you to pull forward when leaving.
Any spot without concern for location.
A parking lot with many tight corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: A spot that allows you to pull forward when leaving.
questions.explanation: When parking a double or triple, only park in spots where you can pull forward to exit. Avoid parking spots that require you to back up to leave.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid hitting a hazard on the road?

options.text: Always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.
Never swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Sometimes turning away from a hazard is safer than trying to stop. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can stop completely.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?

options.text: Press down the brake pedal.
Lift the brake pedal toward you.
Push in the brake knob.
Pull out the brake knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop an air-braked vehicle, push the brake pedal down. Control the pressure so the vehicle stops smoothly and safely.

questions.question: What happens if only one axle has anti-lock brakes?

options.text: It will not make a difference in braking.
It will provide better control when braking.
It will likely cause the air brakes to fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will provide better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even if only one axle has anti-lock brakes, you will have more braking control than if you had no anti-lock brakes at all.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
If there is empty space in the truck.
If hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle is carrying hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the outside of any vehicle carrying hazardous materials. They show what class of materials are being carried and warn others of any dangers.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver?

options.text: Quickly pass the vehicle.
Keep a safe distance from the vehicle.
Follow the vehicle closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you notice a distracted driver, give them plenty of space and maintain a safe following distance.

questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, you should know that:

options.text: Bobtails stop very easily.
Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no trailer attached. Bobtails need a longer distance to stop than tractors pulling loaded trailers.

questions.question: Brakes can go out of adjustment quickly when:

options.text: They are hot.
It is winter time.
They are used often.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hot.
questions.explanation: Hot brakes lose adjustment quickly. Check your brakes regularly. Brakes must work well and be properly adjusted for safe control.

questions.question: After a vehicle starts, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should go off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: When a trailer's wheels lock up:

options.text: The trailer will be easy to drive.
The trailer may swing around.
The vehicle will keep steering control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may swing around.
questions.explanation: A trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles if its wheels lock up. This happens especially with light trailers.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to save time.
Is recommended on long trips.
Distracts the driver.
Is required to watch the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Distracts the driver.
questions.explanation: Do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Anything that takes your attention away from driving is a distraction.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
Honk your horn.
Not use a turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: When passing a pedestrian or another vehicle, assume they do not see you.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Usually sees hazards more slowly.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually sees hazards more slowly.
questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see road hazards slower than focused drivers, or they miss them completely.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second trailer, the trailer height should be ____ the center of the fifth wheel.

options.text: Level with
Slightly higher than
Slightly lower than

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Cannot be used with air brakes.
Should only be used on dry pavement.
Can help you stay in control when braking.
Should only be used if all axles have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS works with air brakes. ABS helps keep control and stops wheels from locking up during hard braking on slippery surfaces. ABS helps even if only one axle has it.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts should be:

options.text: Loosened.
Checked for tightness.
Cleaned with a brush.
Left alone and not inspected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for tightness.
questions.explanation: Check all belts for tightness and wear. Learn how much movement is correct for each belt.
